Best 5 Premium Hot Wheels Cars in 2026: Porsche, Ferrari and McLaren Reign Supreme
42 photos
Photo: autoevolution
Black Friday is just around the corner, and I had almost forgotten this “celebration” existed in the first place. That’s because I never take part in it, as I’ve spent enough years in the industry to realize what it’s all about. There’s only only one category of products I might be interested in.
Yes, I’m talking about diecast collectibles. Two of the biggest retailers in my area have announced discounts of up to 70% from the model’s original price. I’ll believe it when I’ll see it. I know a good price when I see one, as I spend a lot of time looking at the market.
There’s always a diecast-focused distributor who needs to go ahead with a clearance and will sell the cars for less than he paid for them in the first place. And there’s always one “enthusiast” (read scalper) that realizes he shouldn’t have gone knee deep in the “business” in the first place.
Anyway, think of that as my Sunday Hot Wheels collecting tip. The real reason I started writing this story is because I wanted to let you know what I think are the best 5 premium Hot Wheels cars in 2026.
I won’t be talking about Elite 64 and the Red Line Club for now, as there might be a few surprises left in there. Instead, I’ll be focusing on five collections that have already revealed their complete line-up to us by now.
Pop Culture: 2022 Porsche 911 GT3 RS Photo: autoevolution Now, I’ve thought about several different ways of “nominating” the Top 3 items for each category. Of course this will all be subjective, and your Top 3 can look completely different to mine. I actually encourage to let me know what your favorites are, as I’m always curious to see how Mattel’s products land with other people. Back to Pop Culture : we have seen six mixes this year, which translates to a total of 30 tiny cars.
Right off the bat, some of them don’t belong on this list as they’re repeat models from previous years. I’m talking about the Lincoln Continental from the Matrix, the Guinevere Van from Onward, the Simpsons Family Car and all the other models that aren’t even real cars. So where does that leave us? Well, if this list would have been called “The Most Hyped Cars of 2026”, the Godzilla-themed Nissan Skyline GT-R (BNR34) would have taken the win.
I’ve seen some “entrepreneurs” asking as much as $480 for these, which is downright ridiculous and offensive for a non-RLC, non-limited collectible. The 1983 BMW 733i was pretty hot, especially since it was a brand-new casting. The Forza-themed Audi 90 quattro was new to Premium, but maybe not as desirable for most.
I’d love a closer look at the James Bond -powered Lotus Esprit Turbo, and it might have won today’s “award” if it had different wheels. My vote goes to Ronald Wong’s 2022 Porsche 911 GT3 RS that pays tribute to Gran Turismo. I’m not 100% happy with the color combo, but that issue will be solved with next year’s Canyon Warriors iteration.
Boulevard: Ferrari Enzo Photo: Lamley Group The choice is a bit more complicated for the Boulevard series, despite it only having five mixes throughout the year. That adds up to 25 models, but there are no repeat ones to think of. There are also no “wacky racers”, if you know what I mean. Let’s have a quick look at the new variations for existing castings first.
The 2001 BMW M3 GTR has definitely reached new heights for its second release, and I haven’t been able to find the Metalflake Silver release anywhere in the wild. Mix 2 was a real banger, and there’s no doubt the HKS-themed Nissan Skyline GT-R (R32) Pandem was the hottest car there.
I still enjoyed the '69 Ford Torino Talladega and the Lamborghini Gallardo LP 570-4 Superleggera, and it just so happens that the latter two are the only ones I haven’t parted ways with yet. I haven’t bought a single car from Mix 3, but the nostalgic Datsun King Cab Baja Custom is my favorite there. Mix 4 was pretty big, and I’ll say it here: everyone on the planet wanted to have the Ferrari Enzo!
It’s one of eight new castings for 2026, and I even broke my own rule for it by paying 50% more than its regular retail price just so I could park it next to the F50. It was definitely a close call between the iconic supercar and the classic JDM racer!
Car Culture: Ferrari Testarossa Photo: autoevolution Car Culture further complicates the situation by featuring 48 different cars throughout the year. I will make it easier for myself here and take eight of them out of the equation right off the bat, as I’ve never even seen one of the Chase items up close. To me, it’s almost as if they don’t even exist in the first place. There’s a 5-piece set of them featuring the Datsun, Chevy, BMW , Mercedes and Nissan for sale on eBay for $1,850 if you feel otherwise.
Looking back at Japan Historics 5, it looks more enticing now than it did the first time I saw it in a toy store. I bought the least exciting one there (the Datsun 620), but I’m not sure I’d add either one of them on today’s shortlist. This might sound controversial to some of you, but the Lancia Delta S4 from Thrill Climbers is definitely going into my Top 5 for 2026.
If it had a removable hatch like you’d get on the 787B, it would have won hands down. The green BMW M3 from Power Trip was decent but not award-worthy decent. The new 1994 NISMO 270R (S14) turned out to be a peg-warmer in my area, and I’m under the impression the Porsche 993 GT2 under performed just as well.
The Ferrari Testarossa has to be a Top 3 collectible, and I’m putting it up there with the Aerostyles 2008 Audi A4 Touring Car. Vintage Racing and Road Trip haven’t provided any entries for my list, and I’m not 100% sure about Deutschland Design either. Now, I want to say the DTM-spec Audi is the winner, but I’d only do that just to avoid making this list look like a Ferrari-focused party. Do you agree the Testarossa reign supreme for Car Culture this year?
Team Transport: Team #95 (Porsche Cayenne and Porsche 944 Turbo) Photo: Lamley Group I seem to have already overextended myself here, so I’ll try to be brief moving forward. Mattel gave us four mixes of Team Transport this year for a total of 12 teams, plus the bonus Walmart Legends Tour Exclusive release.
It might be fair to go for a double award here, as each package contains two vehicles. So picking just one item doesn’t make perfect sense, but could still be a way to go about I. We only had three new castings all years.
The Mercedes-Benz 300 SLR arrived in Mix 2, Terra-Torque was a hauler in Mix 3, and the 2008 Porsche Cayenne had the same role in Mix 4. I know everyone went crazy for Team #97, as Rexy tends to get that sort of reaction from the audience.
But the new iteration of the Porsche 911 GT3 R (992) is just too similar to the First Edition of the casting to win my vote. If I had to pick just one vehicle, I would likely go for the Terra-Torque truck. However, when it comes to complete teams, #95 is the one for me as the appeal of two Porsches in one set is too strong for me to resist.
Premium Collector Sets: 1997 McLaren F1 GTR Photo: Lamley Group I initially thought about including the Car Culture 2-Packs in this list. We had four mixes there, with a total of 24 cars. Half of them were either identical or similar to previous releases, which is why I decided to “disqualify” the series from this “ceremony”.
If I had included, the Maserati MC12 would have won hands down. The Premium Collector Sets have been around for seven years now, and Mattel has gotten everyone used to seeing four packages a year. I won’t nominate the best package, as the mix inside is almost never perfect.
That means I’ll focus on the best out of 16 models instead. I think the 1957 Jeep FC from Off-Road was nice, but not amazing. The Toyota package didn’t bring anything particularly new to the table, while the Mooneyes 1934 Ford Hot Rod was pretty stunning. It just can’t compete with the Gulf-powered 1997 McLaren F1 GTR.
The hype around it was so insane, that I don’ even mind not being able to buy one for my collection. These are my favorite Premium Hot Wheels this year, I’ll be back with a look at the basic lines, Elite 64 and the Red Line Club later this month or in December the latest.
